title: The storm (Mark 4:35–41)
hookLine: he sleeps in the boat, they wake him, he says to the sea peace, be still

cards: Evening on the Lake of Galilee. After a long day of teaching, Jesus says: let us pass over to the other side. They push off.
Some of these men have fished this lake their whole lives. Then the wind comes. The lake sits low, ringed by hills, and storms can drop onto it suddenly and hard.
Waves break over the side. The boat is filling. Experienced fishermen are bailing and shouting.
And Jesus? Mark says he was in the back of the boat, asleep on a cushion. Asleep.

teach.h: DON'T YOU CARE THAT WE PERISH?
teach.b: They wake him, and what they say is honest, and a little angry. In the Douay-Rheims: "Master, doth it not concern thee that we perish?" Don't you care?
It's one of the most human prayers in the Bible. Jesus gets up, rebukes the wind, and says to the sea: "Peace, be still."
In Greek it's two short commands, the words you'd use to quiet a barking dog or a shouting man: be silent, be muzzled. He talks to the storm as if it's a creature that has to obey.
The wind drops, and there's a great calm. Then he turns to them: why are you fearful? Have you not faith yet?
Here's the twist. Before the storm, they were afraid of the weather.

After the calm, Mark says, they feared exceedingly, and said to each other: who is this, that both wind and sea obey him? The calm scares them more than the storm did. The Church has always seen itself in this boat.

teach.h: THE NAVE — THE CHURCH AS A BOAT.
teach.b: The main part of a church building is called the nave, from the Latin navis, a ship: the Church is the boat on the water, full of frightened people, with Christ aboard.
He doesn't promise there'll be no storms. He's in the boat when it comes.
This week has been full of people who reached him in trouble: friends on a roof, a tax collector, a woman at a well, a soldier, a woman in a crowd, a father.
Today it's his own friends, bailing water, shouting: don't you care?

how: Catholics hear the calming of the storm at Sunday Mass, and the image of the Church as a boat runs through Catholic art and preaching; the nave of a church takes its name from the Latin for ship.

o: a sudden squall on the lake, calmed by a word
the wind that shook the house at Pentecost
the flood God sent in the days of Noah

games.q: what's inside the story — tap the pairs.
p: where Jesus slept in the storm
what he said to the sea

s: the disciples are calm once the storm stops
they fear exceedingly and ask each other: who is this?
Jesus is asleep when the storm hits
in the back of the boat, on a cushion.

games.q: you're in the boat. the waves are breaking over the side, and Jesus is asleep. what do you do?
o: let him sleep and keep bailing.
wake him and ask if he even cares.
jump out and swim for shore.
games.why: they wake him: “Master, doth it not concern thee that we perish?” he rises and says to the sea: “Peace, be still.”

practice: Let one worry come, the one that's been sloshing around all week; don't bail, just notice the waves.
Breathe in for four and out for six, and on each out-breath let the words come silently, peace, be still, not ordering the worry away, just letting it quiet a little.
If you pray, you can wake him, like they did, with your honest question.

wordCard.voice: The storm. A boat filling with water, a teacher asleep, and three words to the sea. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: be silent, be muzzled. Mark's words for what Jesus said to the sea.

carryVoice: Your line: peace, be still. Next week: the stories he told, starting with a sower. That's week six.
